title: Ishwara Pranidhana
tagline: Surrender to the divine — letting go into trust
description: Surrender to the divine — letting go into trust

sutra.transliteration: Sutra The three pillars of practice.
sutra.meaning:
Discipline in practice, self-study, study of the scriptures and surrender to God are the acts of yoga.
Yoga reduces suffering and prepares one for meditation.

sections.insight: I need to be committed to make progress
sections.reflectionPrompt:
Can I make a commitment to myself?


Effort + awareness + surrender = growth.	Am I balanced in effort?
sections.meditation: 10 mins meditation with intention to be comitted
sections.gurudevInsight:
"""""""Krishna tells Arjuna, Arjuna, you know, who is really intelligent & clever? Arjuna says no.
“One who sees silence in activity & activity in silence, he is the intelligent person. How do
you see silence in activity & activity in silence? It needs sharpness of awareness, alertness,
keenness which come when there is skill in your activity. And the skill in
activity is Yoga, Kriya yoga – Yoga of action. What is it? It comprises of 3 parts.
1.Tapas: Tapas is endurance, acceptance - You decide on your own to do some action which is not usual, that is Tapas. 
2.Swadhyaya, being alert, self-study, observing the breath, observing the emotions, thoughts,
what all happens inside you – observing, studying yourself i.e. swadhaya.
3.Ishwarapranidhana: devotion to the Divine, love to the Divine- these three things together
makes kirya yoga."

sutra.meaning: Cleanliness, contentment, discipline, self-study, surrender, these fixed observances refine inner life.
sutra.padaVibhaga: śauca | santoṣa | tapaḥ | svādhyāya | īśvara-praṇidhānāni | niyamāḥ
sutra.wordMeanings: śauca = purity; santoṣa = contentment; tapaḥ = austerity; svādhyāya = self-study; īśvara-praṇidhānāni = surrender to God; niyamāḥ = observances

sections.insight: There is always scope for improvement in following all of these Niyamas
sections.reflectionPrompt: Which one needs special attention from me?
sections.practice: Focus on one at a time. Which one is particularly challenging for me.
sections.journalPrompt: What changes was I inspired to make in my life?
sections.gurudevInsight: a) Shaucha b) Santosha c) Tapas d) Swadhaya e) Ishwara Pranidhana are niyamas

sutra.meaning: From  profound  meditation upon the Divine comes the perfection of continuous effortless linkage of the attention to that Divinity.
sutra.wordMeanings: samādhi = absorption; siddhiḥ = perfection; īśvara-praṇidhānāt = from surrender to God

sections.insight: The power of samadhi comes to him who takes refuge in the Divine.
sections.reflectionPrompt: Surrender to God brings perfection in samadhi. Can I surrender to the Divine?
sections.practice: sit for meditation with the intention of total surrender
sections.gurudevInsight:
"Love of the God- surrender
to the Lord will complete the Process. Without Love, self-study becomes another dry stuff.
Without surrender, self-study is not charming. Without devotion, without love, spiritual path
becomes very dry like a Styrofoam – its like a cake without sweets, a pudding without sweetness."
